trip.title: Utah Canyon Country
trip.subtitle: From the Rockies into the Red Rock West

days.title: Fort Collins → Black Canyon → Montrose, CO

lodging.checkin: Check in Mon Oct 12 from 3:00 PM · check out Tue Oct 13 by 11:00 AM

options.name: Home in Montrose (Airbnb, hosted by Cat)
options.note: 1700 American Way. Two bedrooms, one bath, grill. Host sends check-in instructions the morning you arrive; shoes off at the door, and it is a quiet family home rather than a party house

items.title: Depart Fort Collins
items.detail: Load the car the night before. Long day, but it ends with a national park in it rather than just mileage.

items.title: Drive to Fairplay
items.detail: I-25 south, around Denver on C-470, then US-285 over Kenosha Pass (10,001 ft) into South Park — a treeless basin the size of a county.

items.title: Fairplay — first real break
items.detail: A 19th-century mining town at 9,950 ft. Gas, coffee and a proper stretch before the next stretch of mountains.

items.title: Drive to Gunnison over Monarch Pass
items.detail: US-285 over Trout Creek Pass, down the Arkansas headwaters past Salida, then US-50 crosses the Continental Divide at Monarch Pass (11,312 ft).

items.title: Lunch in Gunnison
items.detail: A college town on the Gunnison River and the last substantial place to eat before the canyon. Fuel up here too.

items.title: Drive to Black Canyon — South Rim
items.detail: US-50 west through the Curecanti reservoirs, then CO-347 climbs six miles to the rim. Directly on the way now that you sleep in Montrose.

items.title: Black Canyon of the Gunnison — South Rim
items.detail: A gorge so narrow and so deep that parts of the floor get half an hour of sunlight a day. Drive the South Rim Road and stop at Gunnison Point, Chasm View, Painted Wall (the tallest cliff in Colorado at 2,250 ft) and Sunset View. All short paved walks from the car park.
items.flag: The South Rim Road stays open until the first significant snowfall — usually mid-November, but it is weather-dependent, not a fixed date. The visitor center runs 9:00 AM–4:00 PM from Oct 1 with a lunch closure at 12:00–12:30. Check nps.gov/blca before you commit to the stop.

items.title: Drive to Montrose
items.detail: Back down CO-347 and a few miles west. Twenty miles — the shortest end-of-day drive on the whole trip.

items.title: Arrive Montrose — check in
items.detail: 1700 American Way. Check-in from 3:00 PM, so you are well inside it. Two bedrooms, one bath, a grill in the yard. The host asks for shoes off at the door.

items.title: Dinner in Montrose
items.detail: A real town with real supermarkets — the last easy shopping until St George. Stock the cooler tonight.

tips: Leave by 6:30 — the Black Canyon overlooks are the point of the day.
Black Canyon entry is covered by the America the Beautiful and Senior passes.
Two Continental Divide crossings today, Kenosha and Monarch. Check cotrip.org the morning you go.
Montrose sits at 5,800 ft, so the first night is a gentle one for altitude. Ouray tomorrow is 7,800 and you are only passing through.
Pack the cooler the night before; South Park and the Gunnison stretch are thin on services.

momNotes.text: Question mark next to the Strater Hotel — wants to talk it through before booking.

stops.name: Black Canyon of the Gunnison — South Rim

days.title: Montrose → Million Dollar Highway → Telluride → Dolores

lodging.chosen: Wrangler's Roost Family Suite — 27660 Road P
lodging.checkin: Check in Tue Oct 13 from 4:00 PM · check out Wed Oct 14 by 11:00 AM

options.name: Room in Dolores — Wrangler's Roost Family Suite (Airbnb, hosted by JanElle and Todd)
options.note: 27660 Road P, Dolores. A family suite rather than an entire house; the hosts send the address and arrival detail closer to the date

items.title: Check out of Montrose
items.detail: Check-out is 11:00, so there is no rush, but the Million Dollar Highway is better early with the light behind you.

items.title: Drive south to Ouray
items.detail: US-550 down the Uncompahgre valley. The San Juans build in the windscreen the whole way and Ouray appears suddenly, wedged into its box canyon.

items.title: Drive the Million Dollar Highway south
items.detail: US-550 out of Ouray on a shelf blasted into the wall of the Uncompahgre Gorge — no guardrail, a sheer drop off the passenger side, and Bear Creek Falls dropping under the road at mile 2.
items.flag: Red Mountain Pass is maintained all winter but can close on short notice in an early storm, and it is a serious road in bad weather. Check cotrip.org before you set off. If it is closed you lose nothing else — turn around and head straight for Telluride.

items.title: Red Mountain Pass and the Ironton overlooks
items.detail: Turn around at the pass (11,018 ft). The Red Mountain mining district on the way up is rust-orange rock with wooden headframes still standing in the trees. Silverton beyond it is another 45 minutes each way and the good part ends here.

items.title: Drive back down to Ouray
items.detail: The same shelf road northbound, which is the better direction for the gorge — the drop is now on the driver’s side and the town appears below you.

items.title: Box Cañon Falls, Ouray
items.detail: A 285-foot waterfall roaring inside a limestone slot barely wider than your shoulders, reached by a steel walkway bolted to the canyon wall. About ten minutes of walking. Roughly $8 adult, $7 senior, $6 for ages 4–17.

items.title: Drive to Telluride
items.detail: North to Ridgway, then west and south up the San Miguel valley. Gentler than the morning — no cliff edges — and the aspens should still be turning.

items.title: Lunch in Telluride
items.detail: The main street runs straight at a wall of mountains with Bridal Veil Falls at the end of it. You are parked for the afternoon.

items.title: Telluride and the free gondola
items.detail: A free gondola climbs 1,750 ft over the ridge to Mountain Village and back, running 6:30 AM to midnight through Oct 25. Fifteen minutes each way and a stroller rolls straight on.

items.title: Drive to Dolores
items.detail: CO-145 south over Lizard Head Pass, then down the Dolores River. The house is on the county grid south-west of town, twenty minutes closer to Mesa Verde than Dolores itself.

items.title: Arrive Dolores — check in
items.detail: 27660 Road P. Check-in from 4:00 PM. The hosts live on site and will meet you.

items.title: Dinner in Dolores
items.detail: A small town on the river with a couple of good options. Cortez is fifteen minutes south if you want more choice.

tips: Two passes above 10,000 ft today. Check cotrip.org before Red Mountain in the morning and again before Lizard Head in the afternoon.
Red Mountain Pass is maintained all winter but can close on short notice in an early storm. If it is shut you lose nothing else — turn around and head straight for Telluride.
Drive times today are padded above what routing engines report; US-550 and CO-145 are twisty mountain highways and the machines are optimistic about them.
Dolores is tiny. Do the desert shopping in Cortez tomorrow morning, not here.

days.title: Dolores → Mesa Verde → Kayenta

lodging.checkin: Check in Wed Oct 14 from 3:00 PM · check out Thu Oct 15 by 11:00 AM · lockbox self check-in

options.name: Bright & Spacious, family-friendly home in Kayenta (Airbnb, hosted by Divine)
options.note: 126 Arrowhead Drive, in town. Thirty minutes south of the Monument Valley overlook and, more usefully, twenty-six miles closer to Page than staying at the valley would be. The host warns that GPS will not find it and cell service is unreliable, so carry the printed directions

items.title: Depart Dolores
items.detail: Breakfast at the suite, away by 7:50. Today has one long transit leg in the middle of it.

items.title: Drive to Mesa Verde — Chapin Mesa
items.detail: County roads to US-160, then the long climb up the mesa. Being out on Road P rather than in Dolores town saves twenty minutes of this.

items.title: Mesa Verde National Park — Chapin Mesa
items.detail: Start at the museum, then the Mesa Top Loop, then the Cliff Palace overlook. Ranger-led cliff dwelling tours are ticketed and sell out — book ahead or view from the rim, which is still remarkable.

items.title: Drive down off the mesa to Cortez
items.detail: The 20-mile park road again in reverse, then ten minutes west.

items.title: Lunch in Cortez
items.detail: Back down at the highway. The last proper town for a long while — do the desert shopping here, and fuel up, because services thin out badly once you turn south.

items.title: Drive to Goosenecks
items.detail: US-160 west then US-163 south, crossing into Utah. Long, empty, beautiful. Skipping Goosenecks makes this a straight run to Monument Valley: 125 mi, 2 hr 15 min.

items.title: Goosenecks State Park
items.detail: A thousand-foot overlook onto the San Juan River folded back on itself five times. Twenty minutes at the rail is enough, and there are no guardrails to speak of — hold onto the three-year-old.

items.title: Drive to the Monument Valley overlook
items.detail: UT-261 south to US-163. The Mittens come into view about ten minutes out and it is worth the whole drive.

items.title: Wildcat Trail and the Mittens overlook
items.detail: The overlook behind the visitor center gives you the postcard — East Mitten, West Mitten and Merrick Butte — for the price of walking to the rim. Sign in at the visitor center if anyone wants to start the 3.2-mile Wildcat loop; there is not time to finish it today.

items.title: Drive to Kayenta
items.detail: South on US-163 with the monuments in the mirror, then west on US-160 into town. Be out through the park gate by 5:00 — that is when it closes.

items.title: Navajo Code Talker Exhibit, Kayenta
items.detail: A genuine museum of Navajo Code Talker history — uniforms, radios, letters — housed, improbably, inside the Burger King on US-160 as you come into town. Free, twenty minutes, and the best short history stop of the trip. Worth ringing ahead; it has kept irregular hours.

items.title: Arrive Kayenta — check in
items.detail: 126 Arrowhead Drive. Lockbox entry. Check-in is from 3:00 PM, so arriving now is fine.

items.title: Dinner in Kayenta
items.detail: Amigo Cafe is the local institution — Navajo and Mexican, and it closes earlier than you expect. Blue Coffee Pot is the other one. Kayenta also has the last full supermarket before Page.

tips: The Tribal Park runs winter hours from Oct 1: gates open 8:00 AM, close 5:00 PM, last Scenic Drive entry 2:30 PM. Arriving at 4:15 works for the visitor-center overlook; it does not work for the 17-mile loop.

Sunset is 6:46 PM and the park shuts at 5:00, so there is no sunset from inside it. If you want one, US-163 north of the park is free and open all night — Forrest Gump Point is twenty-five minutes up the road — but it puts you into Kayenta near 8:00 PM on unlit roads with open-range livestock.
THE HOST WARNS GPS WILL NOT FIND THE HOUSE and there may be no cell signal. Print the written directions before you leave Colorado. The coordinates are N 36°42.784, W 110°14.931.
Mesa Verde's Wetherill Mesa road usually closes by mid-October, but Chapin Mesa — the part you want — stays open.
Book the Cliff Palace tour at recreation.gov ($5/person). It fills fast even in October.

Park entry at Mesa Verde is covered by America the Beautiful / Senior Pass. Monument Valley is a Navajo Tribal Park and is NOT covered — check the posted rate at navajonationparks.org before you go, it has changed recently.

momNotes.text: Circled "Senior Pass" against the Mesa Verde section — she has one, so park entry is covered. She circled it again on Days 5, 9, 11 and the packing list.
Star next to The View Hotel — her pick for Monument Valley. It had no availability for Oct 14; the booking is a house in Kayenta, thirty minutes south.
Question mark next to the guided Jeep tours. Decided against on cost — the Wildcat Trail covers the valley on foot for the price of the entry fee.

days.title: Kayenta → Lake Powell → Zion → Washington, UT

lodging.chosen: Casitas at Sienna Hills — 1902 E Respite Lane, Washington
lodging.checkin: Check in Thu Oct 15 from 4:00 PM · check out Mon Oct 19 by 11:00 AM

options.name: Casitas at Sienna Hills — "Huge Pool & Hot Tub | By Zion & St George | 1902SH" (Airbnb, St George Rentals)
options.note: 1902 E Respite Lane, Washington, just off Washington Parkway at I-15 exit 13. Three bedrooms, 2.5 baths, sleeps 10; a Pack ’n Play is provided. Heated community pool and hot tub year-round, five minutes’ walk. Washer and dryer

items.title: Breakfast at the house and load the car
items.detail: Sunrise is 7:28. You have a kitchen, and the next food is ninety miles away in Page.

items.title: Drive to Glen Canyon Dam, Page
items.detail: US-160 west then US-98 across the Navajo Nation — big, empty, fast road. Fill the tank in Kayenta.
items.flag: Page, AZ does not observe daylight saving but the Navajo Nation does. Driving from Kayenta into Page you gain an hour; crossing back into Utah you lose it again. Phones change on their own — trust the clock, not your sense of elapsed time. All times on this page are Utah time.

items.title: Glen Canyon Dam and the Carl Hayden Visitor Center
items.detail: The dam that made Lake Powell: 710 feet of concrete holding back the Colorado, with the lake on one side and the green river canyon on the other. The visitor center is free, open 8:00–5:00, and has restrooms, air conditioning and a relief map of the whole canyon system — a soft landing after a hundred miles.

items.title: Horseshoe Bend, Page AZ
items.detail: The famous meander of the Colorado River — not Lake Powell, which is behind the dam. A 1.5-mile round trip over open sand with no shade, $10 per vehicle, and four miles back south of the dam. Worth it, but it is the piece to drop if the morning is running late.

items.title: Drive to Wahweap Overlook
items.detail: Two miles north on US-89, then a signed 0.8-mile gravel road up the hill. Any car can do it.

items.title: Wahweap Overlook — the Lake Powell view
items.detail: This is the view of Lake Powell. Six hundred feet above the water on a bare promontory, looking out over Wahweap Bay and the marina to Castle Rock, Tower Butte and Navajo Mountain, with the dam behind you. Free, outside the fee area, and a two-minute walk from the car.

items.title: Drive to Kanab
items.detail: US-89 north over the Utah line, along the top of the lake past Big Water and Lone Rock, then up through the Vermilion Cliffs.

items.title: Toadstool Hoodoos
items.detail: Mushroom-shaped rocks balancing on thin stems, a flat 1.5-mile round trip from an unmarked US-89 pull-off. Free and almost empty.

items.title: Lunch in Kanab
items.detail: A proper town with real choice. Shop here too: you have a kitchen for the next four days.

items.title: Best Friends Animal Sanctuary, Kanab
items.detail: The largest no-kill sanctuary in the country, in a red-rock canyon north of town. Free but must be booked ahead. Adds about 1 hr 30 min.

items.title: Drive to the Canyon Overlook trailhead
items.detail: US-89 north to Mt Carmel Junction, then UT-9 west through the east entrance. The trailhead is immediately at the far end of the Zion–Mount Carmel tunnel, so it is directly on your way in.

items.title: Canyon Overlook Trail (1 mi RT, moderate)
items.detail: Done today rather than tomorrow, because you drive past the door. A short hike to a magnificent panorama over lower Zion Canyon. Some exposure on one side but well maintained. Parking is very limited — if the pullouts are full, carry on and try again tomorrow morning.

items.title: Drive down to the Zion Visitor Center
items.detail: Back through the tunnel and down the switchbacks into the canyon.

items.title: Pa'rus Trail
items.detail: A 1.7-mile paved, flat trail along the Virgin River from the visitor center — the only trail in Zion open to strollers and bicycles. A gentle first look at the canyon walls.

items.title: Drive to the Casitas
items.detail: UT-9 west out of the canyon, then I-15 south to Washington. The last stretch is easy interstate after a very long day.

items.title: Arrive the Casitas — check in
items.detail: 1902 E Respite Lane. Check-in from 4:00 PM. Four nights here, so unpack properly — this is the only time on the trip you do.

items.title: Dinner in Washington
items.detail: A proper town with real choice. Shop here too: you have a kitchen for the next four days.

tips: Page, AZ does not observe daylight saving but the Navajo Nation does. Driving from Kayenta into Page you gain an hour; crossing back into Utah you lose it again. Phones change on their own — trust the clock, not your sense of elapsed time. All times on this page are Utah time.

Wahweap Overlook is free and needs no pass — it sits outside the Glen Canyon fee area. The Carl Hayden Visitor Center is free too. Horseshoe Bend is the one that charges, $10 per vehicle, and it is run by the city rather than the Park Service.

The Canyon Overlook trailhead sits at the east end of the Zion–Mount Carmel tunnel, directly on the road in from Kanab, which is why it falls today rather than tomorrow. Parking there is very limited — if it is full, keep going and pick it up tomorrow morning.
Fill the tank in Kayenta. It is ninety-six miles to Page and there is nothing in between.
A long day but no longer a punishing one: 7:00 AM to dinner at 6:15, and 252 miles. If it is too much, drop the Pa’rus Trail and you reach the house at 4:15.

momNotes.text: Star and a smiley face next to the Pa'rus Trail — clearly a highlight for her.
Ranked Springdale lodging: Cable Mountain Lodge 1st, Desert Pearl Inn 2nd.

stops.name: Glen Canyon Dam — Carl Hayden Visitor Center

days.title: Zion National Park — Full Day

lodging.chosen: Casitas at Sienna Hills — 1902 E Respite Lane, Washington

items.title: Drive to the Zion Visitor Center
items.detail: UT-9 east from Washington. A later start than the old plan, because Canyon Overlook is already done.

items.title: Park at the Visitor Center and pick up the shuttle
items.detail: The shuttle runs Oct 16 (the Sept 13 – Oct 24 schedule, 7:00 AM to 6:00 PM, every 5–10 minutes), which means private vehicles are not allowed up the Scenic Drive. Strollers must be folded on board. The lot fills mid-morning — if it is full, drop back into Springdale, park there and take the free town shuttle to the pedestrian entrance.

items.title: Shuttle to Zion Lodge — stop 5
items.detail: Roughly halfway up the canyon. The narration is genuinely good.

items.title: Lower Emerald Pools
items.detail: 1.2 miles, paved and flat: a wide trail to a pool beneath a dripping overhang that showers mist on everyone below. The reliable option and the one to build the day around.

items.title: The Zion Lodge lawn
items.detail: Shade, grass and somewhere to put a baby down before lunch. The only patch of it in the canyon.

items.title: Lunch at the Zion Lodge café
items.detail: Right at shuttle stop 5. The only food inside the canyon — anywhere else means riding back out.

items.title: Shuttle to Weeping Rock — stop 7
items.detail: Two stops up the canyon.

items.title: Weeping Rock — check status first
items.detail: 0.4 miles, very easy: a spring seeps through the canyon wall into a hanging garden with a gentle waterfall. The area took a large rockfall in 2019 and the trails above remain on long-term closure; the short trail has reopened and closed repeatedly since. Check the morning of — if it is shut, ride on to the Temple of Sinawava.

items.title: Shuttle to the Temple of Sinawava — last stop
items.detail: The end of the line, past Big Bend and the Court of the Patriarchs.

items.title: Riverside Walk and the Temple of Sinawava
items.detail: The version of the Scenic Drive you actually get in October, narrated, with no parking to fight over. The Riverside Walk is 2.2 miles paved and stroller-friendly if there is energy left.

items.title: Shuttle back down to the Visitor Center
items.detail: The full run back down the canyon. Allow the full 40 minutes — it stops everywhere.

items.title: Drive back to the Casitas
items.detail: UT-9 west and I-15 south. The pool is heated year-round if anyone still has legs.

items.title: Dinner in Washington
items.detail: Back at the house by 5:45. Cook, or take your pick in town.

tips: Zion Visitor Center parking fills mid-morning. Arriving at 8:50 on a Friday is reasonable but not guaranteed — leave at 7:30 if you want certainty.
If the lot is full: park in Springdale and take the free town shuttle to the pedestrian entrance. You lose twenty minutes, not the day.
The shuttle is the only way up the canyon in October. Private cars are barred on the Scenic Drive.
Everything today is on the shuttle, so the car sits at the Visitor Center from 8:50 to 4:55.

momNotes.text: Circled "Senior Pass" again in the Zion notes.
Her circled "Senior Pass" still applies — entry is covered, and the shuttle is free on top of that.

stops.name: Zion Visitor Center — shuttle all day

days.routeNote: Only the two legs shown are driven. Everything inside the canyon is the park shuttle.

days.title: Kolob Canyons → Snow Canyon → back to Washington

lodging.chosen: Casitas at Sienna Hills — 1902 E Respite Lane, Washington

items.title: Drive to Kolob Canyons
items.detail: I-15 north to exit 40. Kolob has its own entrance off the interstate — it is not connected to Zion Canyon by road. No packing up this morning; you are here three more nights.

items.title: Kolob Canyons — Zion's other half
items.detail: A five-mile scenic drive into blood-red finger canyons that most Zion visitors never see. Your Zion pass covers it. Almost no crowds, and the payoff-per-minute is the best in the park. The visitor centre at the entrance closes 12:00–1:00 for lunch, so use the restrooms on the way in.

items.title: Picnic lunch at the Kolob Canyons Viewpoint
items.detail: Tables at the end of the drive looking straight into the canyons. Make it at the house before you leave — there is no food at Kolob at all.

items.title: Drive to Snow Canyon
items.detail: I-15 south past St George, then up and over into the Red Cliffs.

items.title: Snow Canyon State Park
items.detail: Petrified sand dunes the kids can scramble on, black lava tubes, and Jenny's Canyon — a 0.5-mile round trip into a slot barely wider than your shoulders. Ten degrees warmer than Zion and far less busy.

items.title: Drive back to the Casitas
items.detail: Twenty-five minutes east. No check-in, no unpacking.

items.title: The pool and the hot tub
items.detail: Both heated year-round and five minutes on foot. Towels are provided.

items.title: Dinner in Washington
items.detail: Cook, or walk out. Sunset is 6:50.

tips: No check-out and no check-in today — the single biggest gain from basing here for four nights.
The Kolob Canyons visitor centre shuts 12:00–1:00. The scenic drive and viewpoint stay open; only the building closes.
Make the picnic at the house. There is no food at Kolob and nothing between there and Snow Canyon.

momNotes.text: Circled "70–76°F" — she's noting St. George as the warm stretch of the trip.
Question mark next to Inn on the Cliff.

days.title: Washington — Church, Friends, and a Slow Sunday

lodging.chosen: Casitas at Sienna Hills — 1902 E Respite Lane, Washington

items.title: Drive to Redemption Lutheran Church
items.detail: Ten minutes down I-15. The shortest drive to anything on the whole trip.

items.title: Worship at Redemption Lutheran Church
items.detail: An old friend is the pastor here. Arrive a few minutes early to say hello before the service rather than after.

items.title: Lunch with the Raasch family
items.detail: The reason today exists. Give it the whole middle of the day and do not schedule against it.

items.title: Drive back to the house
items.detail: Ten minutes.

items.title: The pool, the hot tub, and nothing
items.detail: The one genuinely unstructured block on the calendar. Laundry, naps, a heated pool five minutes away. Days 8 to 12 are relentless and this afternoon is what makes them survivable.

items.title: Pioneer Park, St. George
items.detail: Only if anyone still has energy — the point of today is that nobody has to. Red sandstone boulders, slots and arches to scramble through, fifteen minutes away and free.

items.title: Dinner — last warm night of the trip
items.detail: About 70°F today. From tomorrow you are at 8,000 ft and it will not be warm again.

tips: Church starts at 10:00 and the drive is ten minutes. This is the only fixed appointment on the trip.
Do the laundry today. It is the midpoint of eleven nights and the next machine is in Cannonville.
Pack for Bryce tonight: from tomorrow you are at 8,000 ft and Tuesday starts near 25°F.

momNotes.text: Wrote "could skip & rest" against the Sunday afternoon. That is now the plan: church, lunch with friends, and nothing compulsory after it.
Underlined "tonight is the last warm night of the trip."

days.title: Washington → Cedar Breaks → Cannonville

lodging.chosen: The House at Pooh Corner — 115 S Kodachrome Rd, Cannonville
lodging.checkin: Check in Mon Oct 19 from 3:00 PM · check out Wed Oct 21 by 11:00 AM · keypad self check-in

options.name: The House at Pooh Corner near Bryce Canyon (Airbnb, hosted by Marshall)
options.note: 115 S Kodachrome Rd, Cannonville. Across the road south of the LDS church, two blocks south of the Sinclair. About 7 miles from the park border and a little over twenty minutes from the entrance station

items.title: Check out of the Casitas
items.detail: Check-out is 11:00, so this is unhurried. Pack the warm layers where you can reach them — you gain 6,000 feet today.

items.title: Drive to Cedar Breaks
items.detail: I-15 north to Cedar City, then UT-14 climbs hard to 10,000 ft — 6,000 feet of gain in seventy miles.

items.title: Cedar Breaks National Monument
items.detail: A half-mile-deep amphitheatre of orange and white rock at 10,350 ft — like Bryce but emptier and a thousand feet higher. Genuinely cold in late October and the rim road can close on early snow; check nps.gov/cebr before committing to the climb.

items.title: Drive to Panguitch
items.detail: Down off the plateau on UT-143 and UT-89. Steep grades and cattle on the road.

items.title: Lunch in Panguitch
items.detail: A 19th-century brick main street and the last real town before Bryce. Also the last reasonably priced petrol — and the last supermarket before Torrey, which has none at all.

items.title: Drive to Red Canyon
items.detail: UT-12 east. The highway runs through two arches cut in the red rock — you drive straight through them.

items.title: Red Canyon (Dixie NF)
items.detail: Bryce-orange hoodoos right beside the highway, with a visitor center and a flat paved path. Free, uncrowded, and a good warm-up for tomorrow.

items.title: Drive to Mossy Cave
items.detail: UT-12 east then a short run down UT-63.

items.title: Mossy Cave Trail
items.detail: A 0.8-mile round trip to a small waterfall and a dripping mossy grotto — inside Bryce Canyon but outside the main amphitheatre, with its own trailhead and no shuttle. The waterfall is the bit she will remember.

items.title: Drive to Cannonville
items.detail: Nine miles south on UT-12 through Tropic. The house is across the road from the LDS church, two blocks south of the Sinclair.

items.title: Arrive Cannonville — check in
items.detail: 115 S Kodachrome Rd. Check-in from 3:00 PM, keypad entry. Two nights.

items.title: Dinner
items.detail: Cannonville has no restaurants. Either cook — you have a kitchen and shopped in Panguitch — or drive five minutes to Tropic.

items.title: Drive to Sunset Point
items.detail: Half an hour up UT-12 and UT-63 to the rim. Cannonville is a real town, not a park-gate strip, and this is what that costs.

items.title: Sunset Point for the sunset
items.detail: Sunset is 6:44. The hoodoos light from the side. Bring every layer you own — it drops below freezing fast once the sun is off the rim.

items.title: Drive back to Cannonville
items.detail: Half an hour down UT-12 in the dark. Deer on the road.

tips: Do the shopping in Panguitch. Cannonville has no restaurants and Torrey, two days from now, has no grocery store at all.
Sunset and sunrise are both a thirty-minute drive from the house. That is the cost of Cannonville — the payoff comes on Day 10, when Kodachrome is fifteen minutes away.
Tropic is five minutes north and has the nearest food.
Keypad entry, so a late arrival is fine.

momNotes.text: Circled the "28–32°F" overnight lows — she wants everyone to have real cold-weather layers for Bryce.

days.title: Bryce Canyon — Full Day from Cannonville

lodging.chosen: The House at Pooh Corner — 115 S Kodachrome Rd, Cannonville

items.title: Drive up to Sunrise Point
items.detail: Half an hour up UT-12 and UT-63 in the dark and the cold. Start the car early and scrape it.

items.title: Sunrise at Sunrise Point
items.detail: Sunrise is 7:47 and the hoodoos catch it first. The single best thirty minutes of the trip, and the reason for the early alarm. Expect low-20s at the rim.

items.title: Breakfast at the rim
items.detail: Brought from the house — flasks, pastries, and a thermos of something hot. Nothing in the park opens this early.

items.title: Queen's Garden Trail (1.8 mi RT, moderate)
items.detail: The gentlest way down among the hoodoos, dropping 320 ft on switchbacks from Sunrise Point. Walking between them beats looking down at them, and this is the one descent a three-year-old can be carried back up.

items.title: Rim Trail: Sunrise to Sunset Point (1.8 mi, easy)
items.detail: Flat, paved, and along the edge the whole way. Do it out and back so you end at the car.

items.title: Drive to Bryce Canyon City
items.detail: Ten minutes out of the park to the strip of restaurants at the junction.

items.title: Lunch in Bryce Canyon City
items.detail: The only cluster of food anywhere near the park.

items.title: Drive south to Rainbow Point
items.detail: Eighteen miles up the plateau to 9,115 ft — the far end of the park road.

items.title: Rainbow Point and the overlooks northbound
items.detail: Drive to the end, then work back down stopping at Agua Canyon, Natural Bridge and Farview. All roadside, all short walks, and the light improves the whole way.

items.title: Drive back to Cannonville
items.detail: Down off the plateau and out to the house.

items.title: Dinner at the house
items.detail: Cook what you bought in Panguitch. Sunset is 6:43 and everyone has been up since six.

tips: Alarm at 6:15. Sunrise Point is thirty minutes away and sunrise is 7:47.
Breakfast comes with you — nothing in the park is open before eight.
Queen's Garden and the Rim Trail both start at Sunrise Point, so the car stays put all morning.
Low-20s at the rim at dawn, near 60°F by afternoon. Layers, not a single warm coat.

momNotes.text: Underlined "Weather changes fast" and "below freezing." Cold is her main concern for the Bryce nights.
Circled "Senior Pass" once more.

days.title: Cannonville → Kodachrome → Scenic Byway 12 → Torrey

lodging.chosen: #6 Home in the Heart of Utah — 125 East Main Street
lodging.checkin: Check in Wed Oct 21 from 3:00 PM · check out Thu Oct 22 by 11:00 AM

options.name: #6 Home in the Heart of Utah (Airbnb, hosted by Danielle and Teresa)
options.note: 125 East Main Street, Torrey. On the main road through town, ten minutes from the Capitol Reef entrance and walkable to what little Torrey has. No grocery store in town — the nearest is Loa, twenty minutes away

items.title: Check out of the house
items.detail: Check-out is 11:00, so this is unhurried. Fill up in Tropic or Escalante — there is no petrol between Boulder and Torrey.

items.title: Drive to Kodachrome Basin
items.detail: Fifteen minutes straight up Kodachrome Road, which the house sits on. This is what Cannonville buys you.

items.title: Kodachrome Basin State Park
items.detail: Sixty-seven sandstone chimneys standing free on the desert floor — nothing else in Utah looks like it. Named by a National Geographic expedition in 1948. The Grand Parade loop is flat and easy.

items.title: Drive Scenic Byway 12 to Boulder
items.detail: The famous stretch: Escalante, then the Hogback — a mile of two-lane road on a knife-edge with the ground falling away on both sides. Slow down and enjoy it.

items.title: Lunch in Boulder
items.detail: Hell’s Backbone Grill is the famous one and needs a booking; Burr Trail Grill is the easy alternative. Boulder had mail delivered by mule until 1940.

items.title: Anasazi State Park Museum, Boulder
items.detail: An excavated Ancestral Puebloan village with a full-size replica dwelling you can walk into. Small, indoors, and a good pause in the middle of a long drive.

items.title: Drive to Capitol Reef
items.detail: Over Boulder Mountain at 9,600 ft, through aspen already turned, then down to the Fremont River.

items.title: Capitol Reef — Fruita district
items.detail: A green Mormon orchard settlement wedged between red cliffs, with a one-room schoolhouse and deer everywhere at dusk. Utterly unlike anywhere else on the trip.

items.title: Gifford Homestead — the pie
items.detail: The homestead sells small fruit pies baked that morning. They sell out. Buy more than you think you need.

items.title: Hickman Bridge Trail (1 mi RT)
items.detail: A steady climb to a 133-ft natural bridge. Worth it if legs allow; skip it without guilt if not.

items.title: Drive to Torrey
items.detail: Fifteen minutes west on UT-24 into town.

items.title: Arrive Torrey — check in
items.detail: 125 East Main Street, right on the main road through town. Check-in from 3:00 PM.

items.title: Dinner in Torrey
items.detail: Torrey has restaurants but no grocery store — the nearest is Loa, twenty minutes away. Sunset is 6:35.

tips: Kodachrome Road runs past the front door, so the park is fifteen minutes away and the day starts without a commute.
No petrol between Boulder and Torrey. Fill up in Escalante.
Torrey has no grocery store. If you need supplies, buy them in Escalante or accept a twenty-minute run to Loa.
The Gifford Homestead pies sell out in the afternoon.

momNotes.text: Wrote "Mmm" next to the Gifford Homestead pies — the apple pie is non-negotiable.
Checked Capitol Reef Resort and Austin's Chuckwagon Motel. Torrey Schoolhouse B&B and Skyridge Inn are real alternatives if you want a third choice.

days.title: Capitol Reef → Goblin Valley → Arches

lodging.chosen: Castle View town home — 3368 E La Camino Dr
lodging.checkin: Check in Thu Oct 22 from 4:00 PM · check out Fri Oct 23 by 10:00 AM · keypad self check-in

options.name: Castle View — 3 bed / 2 bath town home (Airbnb, Moab Lodging Vacation Rentals)
options.note: 3368 E La Camino Dr, four miles south-east of Moab centre and about thirty-five minutes from Balanced Rock. Keypad entry, which is what makes a 7:20 PM arrival workable. Note the 10:00 AM check-out — an hour earlier than the other stays, and the drive home is long

items.title: Depart Torrey — UT-24 east
items.detail: An early start buys you the whole afternoon in Arches, which is the point of today.

items.title: Drive to Goblin Valley
items.detail: UT-24 east across the San Rafael Swell — empty, strange country the whole way.

items.title: Goblin Valley State Park
items.detail: A valley floor covered in thousands of squat mushroom-shaped hoodoos, and the rarest thing in any park: you are allowed to leave the trail and let children loose to climb on them. This is the best ninety minutes of the trip for a three-year-old.

items.title: Little Wild Horse Canyon
items.detail: A genuine slot canyon fifteen minutes from Goblin Valley, narrow enough to touch both walls. The full loop is eight miles, but the good part starts immediately and an hour in and out is worthwhile. Realistically it costs 2 hr 30 min with the drive — which comes straight out of the Arches afternoon. Never enter if there is any chance of rain.

items.title: Drive to Green River
items.detail: North out of Goblin Valley to I-70.

items.title: Lunch in Green River
items.detail: A highway town on the river, and the only real food between Goblin Valley and Moab. Fuel up here.

items.title: Canyonlands NP — Island in the Sky
items.detail: Mesa Arch framing the canyon, and Grand View Point looking two thousand feet down into the Green River gorge. Genuinely world-class — and it is an hour and a quarter out from Green River plus two hours there plus an hour back to Arches. That is the whole Arches afternoon. This is the fork in the road: take Canyonlands instead of Arches, not as well as it.

items.title: Dead Horse Point State Park
items.detail: A 2,000-foot overlook onto a gooseneck of the Colorado, on the same spur road out to Canyonlands. Only worth it if you have already chosen that road — on its own it is a 1 hr 40 min detour for a single view.

items.title: Drive to Arches — Park Avenue
items.detail: I-70 east then US-191 south. The park entrance is five miles north of Moab and Park Avenue is the first stop inside it.

items.title: Arches — Park Avenue and Courthouse Towers
items.detail: Start at the bottom of the park and work up. Park Avenue is a canyon of vertical sandstone slabs standing in rows like buildings; the overlook takes five minutes and the trail down into it is a flat mile if you want it.

items.title: Drive up to Balanced Rock
items.detail: The park road climbs past the Petrified Dunes with the La Sal Mountains behind them.

items.title: Balanced Rock and the Windows section
items.detail: A 3,600-ton boulder on a slender pedestal, then the Windows: North and South Window and Turret Arch, all reached by short flat gravel paths from one car park. The highest density of arches in the park and the easiest walking — this is the heart of the visit.

items.title: Drive to the Delicate Arch viewpoint
items.detail: Ten minutes north, then a short spur east.

items.title: Delicate Arch viewpoint
items.detail: The famous one. The hike to stand under it is 3 miles round trip up open slickrock with no shade and a sheer drop at the end — not with a three-year-old and a newborn. The lower viewpoint is a flat 100 yards from the car park and shows you the arch across the canyon.

items.title: Drive back to Balanced Rock
items.detail: Ten minutes back down the park road.

items.title: Picnic dinner at the Balanced Rock picnic area
items.detail: There are tables here with the rock right above you. Eating in the park rather than driving back to Moab is what buys you the golden hour — pick the food up in Green River at lunch and carry it. No water at these tables, so bring your own.

items.title: Golden hour at the Windows
items.detail: Sunset is 6:30. The last half hour of light on the Windows is the best light in the park, and by then almost everyone else has driven out to dinner. Five minutes back down the road from the picnic area.

items.title: Drive to the Moab town home
items.detail: Out of Arches in the dark and four miles south-east of town. Google puts it at thirty-five minutes.

items.title: Arrive at the Moab town home
items.detail: 3368 E La Camino Dr. Keypad entry, so a 7:20 arrival after the longest day of the trip is fine — the host sends the code before you travel.

tips: Arches gets the whole afternoon on purpose — 1:00 PM to 6:45 PM, finishing at golden hour in the Windows.
Canyonlands is the fork: it costs the Arches afternoon almost exactly. Pick one. Dead Horse Point sits on the same spur road.
Carry dinner out of Green River. Eating at the Balanced Rock picnic tables is what buys you the last light instead of driving to Moab for it.
Goblin Valley entry ~$25/vehicle — a state park, not covered by the Senior Pass or the park pass.
Closed-toe shoes for Goblin Valley; the sandstone shreds bare feet.
No timed entry permit required for Arches in late October.

momNotes.text: Circled "Pack a full lunch" — even more true now that Goblin Valley is on this leg. Nothing between Torrey and Green River.
Circled "Senior Pass" for the Arches entry. Note it does not cover Goblin Valley or Dead Horse Point.

days.title: Moab → Glenwood Canyon → Fort Collins

items.title: Depart Moab
items.detail: Check-out is 10:00 AM, the earliest of the trip, but you are leaving well before it. Pack the car the night before.

items.title: Leave Moab on UT-128 instead of US-191
items.detail: The river road: fifty miles along the Colorado under red cliffs, rejoining I-70 near Cisco. Adds about 45 minutes to a day that is already long, and it is the prettiest road on the trip.

items.title: Drive to Glenwood Springs
items.detail: US-191 north to I-70, then east through Grand Junction and up Glenwood Canyon — the canyon stretch is genuinely spectacular from the interstate.

items.title: Lunch in Glenwood Springs
items.detail: Downtown, five minutes from the caverns tram. Sit down properly — there is a lot of car left.

items.title: Glenwood Caverns Adventure Park
items.detail: A gondola up the canyon wall to cave tours, a viewing platform over the town and an alpine coaster. The cave tour is the part worth booking. The one stop of the day, so it gets the whole afternoon — buy tram tickets ahead, October hours are reduced.

items.title: Drive to Silverthorne
items.detail: I-70 east over Vail Pass. Weather can turn on this stretch in late October — check CDOT before you leave Glenwood.

items.title: Dinner in Silverthorne
items.detail: Two hours from home, which is exactly the right place to stop. Feeding everyone here means the last leg is quiet and dark and nobody is desperate.

items.title: Drive home to Fort Collins
items.detail: I-70 east through the Eisenhower Tunnel, then north. Mostly downhill and mostly asleep.

items.title: Home in Fort Collins
items.detail: Twelve days, five national parks, five state parks, and about 2,100 miles.

tips: Leave Moab no later than 8 AM to reach Glenwood with time for activities.
Glenwood Caverns is the one stop today. It gets the whole afternoon, which is why the day still lands home by 8 PM.
Glenwood Canyon on I-70 is itself spectacular; stop at the Hanging Lake trailhead pullout just to see the canyon walls.
Check CDOT.com for Eisenhower Tunnel / I-70 mountain corridor conditions before departure.

momNotes.text: Wrote "1st choice" next to Glenwood Caverns / King's Row Cave tour — that settles the Caverns-vs-Hot-Springs question in favor of the Caverns.

views.title: The Painted Wall
views.blurb: Colorado's tallest cliff — 2,250 ft of it — from the South Rim road.

views.title: The Million Dollar Highway
views.blurb: US-550 above Ouray, in the aspen colour we are driving up for.

views.title: Cliff Palace
views.blurb: 150 rooms under an overhang, empty since about 1300.

views.title: Goosenecks of the San Juan
views.blurb: The river takes six miles of meander to travel one mile west.

views.title: West Mitten Butte
views.blurb: Monument Valley from the Navajo Tribal Park rim, late afternoon.

views.title: Horseshoe Bend
views.blurb: The Colorado River 1,000 ft below the rim, ten minutes off US-89.

views.title: Lake Powell from Wahweap Overlook
views.blurb: The view of the lake the postcards use — and a five-minute walk from the car.

views.title: The Watchman
views.blurb: From the footbridge by the visitor center, where the Pa'rus Trail starts.

views.title: Kolob Canyons
views.blurb: Zion's quiet north-west corner — a five-mile road and almost no one on it.

views.title: Snow Canyon
views.blurb: Red Navajo sandstone and black lava, twenty minutes from the house.

views.title: Cedar Breaks
views.blurb: A half-mile-deep amphitheatre at 10,000 ft — bring the coats.

views.title: Thor's Hammer, Bryce Canyon
views.blurb: The hoodoo below Sunset Point, and the reason we gave Bryce two days.

views.title: Kodachrome Basin
views.blurb: Sixty-odd sandstone pipes standing up out of the desert floor.

views.title: Fruita, Capitol Reef
views.blurb: A Mormon orchard settlement under the Waterpocket Fold. The pie is real.

views.title: Goblin Valley
views.blurb: Thousands of mushroom rocks you are allowed to walk among — the toddler stop of the trip.

views.title: Dead Horse Point
views.blurb: 2,000 ft above a gooseneck of the Colorado, straight off the car park.

views.title: Delicate Arch
views.blurb: Utah's licence plate. We are viewing it from the lower viewpoint, not the three-mile climb.

views.title: Glenwood Canyon
views.blurb: I-70 threaded through the Colorado River gorge on the way home.

bookings.what: Home in Montrose, CO — night of Oct 12
bookings.notes: Booked. 1700 American Way — two bedrooms, one bath, grill, hosted by Cat. Check in from 3:00 PM Mon Oct 12, out by 11:00 AM.

bookings.what: Wrangler's Roost Family Suite, Dolores, CO — night of Oct 13
bookings.notes: Booked. 27660 Road P, hosted by JanElle and Todd. Check in from 4:00 PM Tue Oct 13, out by 11:00 AM. A family suite rather than a whole house, and it sits on the county grid south-west of Dolores — twenty minutes closer to Mesa Verde than the town is.

bookings.what: Home in Kayenta, AZ — night of Oct 14
bookings.notes: Booked, $271.12, confirmation HMN4JSZQPC. 126 Arrowhead Drive, hosted by Divine. Check in from 3:00 PM Wed Oct 14, out by 11:00 AM. Lockbox self check-in. The host warns GPS will not find the house and there may be no cell signal: print the written directions and note the coordinates N 36°42.784, W 110°14.931. Every night of the trip is now booked.

bookings.what: Casitas at Sienna Hills, Washington, UT — nights of Oct 15–18
bookings.notes: Booked, $936 for four nights. 1902 E Respite Lane, just off Washington Parkway at I-15 exit 13 — three bedrooms, 8 beds, 2.5 baths, heated pool and hot tub. Check in from 4:00 PM Thu Oct 15, out by 11:00 AM Mon Oct 19. The four-night base is what removes three check-ins and two pack-ups from the middle of the trip.

bookings.what: The House at Pooh Corner, Cannonville, UT — nights of Oct 19 & 20
bookings.notes: Booked, $365.11, confirmation HMF98HWCWH. 115 S Kodachrome Rd, hosted by Marshall, keypad entry. Check in from 3:00 PM Mon Oct 19, out by 11:00 AM Wed Oct 21. Cannonville costs half an hour each way to the Bryce rim but puts Kodachrome fifteen minutes from the door.

bookings.what: #6 Home in the Heart of Utah, Torrey, UT — night of Oct 21
bookings.notes: Booked. 125 East Main Street, hosted by Danielle and Teresa. Check in from 3:00 PM Wed Oct 21, out by 11:00 AM. The host warns there is no grocery store in Torrey — the nearest is Loa, twenty minutes away. Buy food in Escalante on the way.

bookings.what: Castle View town home, Moab, UT — night of Oct 22
bookings.notes: Booked, $348.07, through Moab Lodging Vacation Rentals. 3368 E La Camino Dr — three bedrooms, two baths, four miles south-east of town. Check in from 4:00 PM Thu Oct 22, out by 10:00 AM Fri Oct 23 (an hour earlier than every other stay, and the drive home is the second longest of the trip). Keypad entry, which is what makes the 7:20 PM arrival from Arches workable.
No reservation — pay at the gate, about $30 for the group. Ring 970-325-7080 to confirm October hours; the park runs 9:00–5:00 from Oct 15 and slightly longer before that.

bookings.what: Mesa Verde Cliff Palace ranger tour (Oct 14)
bookings.notes: $5/person, recreation.gov. Reduced October schedule and it fills fast. Book a mid-morning slot — you are on site 8:35–11:35 on the drive out to Monument Valley.

bookings.what: Glenwood Caverns — King's Row Cave tour (Oct 23)
bookings.notes: Mom's 1st choice for the final day.

bookings.what: America the Beautiful pass ($80/yr) or Senior Pass
bookings.notes: Mom has a Senior Pass (free lifetime, 62+) — circled it on five separate pages. Covers Arches, Canyonlands, Capitol Reef, Bryce, Zion, Mesa Verde entry. Does NOT cover Monument Valley ($20/vehicle), Snow Canyon ($10/vehicle), Goblin Valley (~$25/vehicle), or Dead Horse Point.

bookings.what: Arrange Sunday lunch with the Raasch family (Oct 18)
bookings.notes: Worship 10:00 AM at Redemption Lutheran, 348 N Bluff St. Reach out well ahead — Sunday mornings are working time for a pastor.

bookings.what: Utah state park entry fees — pay at each gate
bookings.notes: Snow Canyon $10, Goblin Valley ~$25, Dead Horse Point ~$20, plus Goosenecks ~$5 and Kodachrome ~$10 if you take those options. Roughly $55–70 total. A non-resident annual pass runs about $175, so it is NOT worth buying for this route. None of these are covered by the America the Beautiful pass.

bookings.what: Best Friends Animal Sanctuary tour, Kanab (Oct 15)
bookings.notes: Free, but the 90-minute bus tours must be reserved ahead and do fill. Only if Day 4 is the day you pick it — see the three optional stops on that day, of which you should do one.

items: America the Beautiful annual pass, or Mom's Senior Pass — covers entry to Zion, Bryce, Capitol Reef, Arches, Canyonlands and Mesa Verde. The Senior Pass holder has to be in the vehicle and show it.
Cash and a card. Monument Valley Navajo Tribal Park is $20/vehicle and the Utah state park gates vary — a few are cash-only, a few are card-only.
Printed confirmations for the Mesa Verde ranger tour, Glenwood Caverns and anything else timed. Cell signal in the parks is unreliable.
Layers, seriously. Mornings at Bryce are near 25°F; afternoons in the St. George area are near 75°F.
Warm hat, gloves and a real coat for every adult. Bryce Point after dark is below freezing and you will be standing still for half an hour.
Child's warm hat, mittens and puffy coat for the two Bryce days.
Sun hats and sunglasses for everyone, including the kids.
Church clothes for Sunday morning at Redemption Lutheran on Oct 18.
Swimsuits — the Washington house has a heated pool and a hot tub, and you are there four nights.
More toddler clothes than seems reasonable, plus a complete change kept in the car.
Waterproof hiking shoes for the whole family. October trails can be icy in the morning and wet after rain.
Closed-toe shoes for Goblin Valley and Little Wild Horse Canyon — the sandstone destroys sandals and bare feet.
A bag or ziplocs for sandy shoes before they go back in the car.
Trekking poles for the grandparents if they use them; Queen's Garden drops 320 ft on loose rock.
Infant carrier or wrap. Most of the best viewpoints are short walks on uneven ground, not stroller terrain.
Far more diapers and wipes than the trip length suggests. Torrey, Green River and Monument Valley have almost nowhere to restock.
Portable changing mat — many trailhead restrooms have no table.
Feeding supplies and a way to warm a bottle in the car.
Sun shade for the car window and for the carrier. Sunscreen isn't recommended under six months, so shade and long sleeves do the work.
Message each Airbnb host about a cot rather than assuming one, or bring a travel one. Every night of the trip is now an Airbnb.
Saline drops. The air is extremely dry and Bryce sits at 8,000 ft.
Carrier for when she runs out of steam, which will happen at the furthest point from the car.
Stroller for the paved stretches: the Pa'rus Trail, the Bryce Rim Trail, and the short gravel paths at the Arches Windows.
Sand toys for Goblin Valley.
Downloaded shows and audiobooks. There is no signal for most of the driving.
Reusable bottles, a liter per person per hike, plus a couple of gallon jugs in the trunk.

Ten of the eleven nights have a kitchen, so this trip runs on groceries rather than restaurants. Pack a small kit — a sharp knife, a can opener, coffee, oil, salt — and a soft cooler bag for moving leftovers between houses.

Shop in the big towns: Montrose, Cortez, Kanab, Washington/St George, Panguitch and Escalante. Cannonville has no restaurants and Torrey has no grocery store — the nearest is Loa, twenty minutes away.
A cooler. Day 1 and Day 11 both have long stretches with nothing open.
Far more snacks than you think. Mom circled "pack a full lunch" for a reason (M18).
Download offline maps for the whole route before leaving. There is no signal on Byway 12, around Goblin Valley, or through much of the Navajo Nation.
Phone mounts, car chargers and a power bank.
Check the spare tire and pressures before departure. The Little Wild Horse trailhead road is graded dirt and several trailhead pull-offs are rough.
Motion sickness remedy — Monarch Pass, the Million Dollar Highway, Lizard Head Pass and Byway 12 are all winding.
Trash bags. Several of these stops have no bins.
Sunscreen. The October desert sun is still strong, more so at 8,000 ft.
SPF lip balm and a heavy moisturizer. The dryness catches everyone out by about day three.
First aid kit with blister bandages, ibuprofen and antihistamines.
Any prescriptions, with a few days spare in case weather delays you.

Altitude is a real factor for the grandparents: Monarch Pass is 11,312 ft on Day 1, Red Mountain Pass 11,018 ft on Day 2, Ouray sleeps at 7,792 ft and Bryce at 8,000–9,100 ft for two nights. Drink more water than feels necessary.
Headlamps, ideally with a red-light mode so nobody wrecks everyone's night vision at Bryce Point.
A blanket each for the Bryce rim at sunrise and sunset. You'll be stationary in sub-freezing air.
Binoculars — good for the Milky Way at night and the viewpoints by day.
A star chart or app downloaded in advance; there's no signal at Bryce Point.
The good camera for the Monument Valley sunset and the Bryce sunrise, plus spare batteries — cold drains them fast.
